chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The woman may not let down her hair when she washes from the sexual impurity.

key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: Sexual impurity requiring full body wash

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a woman's hair during ghusl from janabah?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies a specific fiqh detail regarding the validity of ghusl for women, addressing the scholarly debate on whether hair must be untied to ensure water reaches the roots. It reflects the Shia juristic view that keeping hair tied does not invalidate the ritual bath, provided water permeates the strands, thereby offering practical ease for women during purification.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The woman may not let down her hair when she washes from the sexual impurity’.
en.sarwar: 16. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah from ibn Muskan from Muhammad al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
It is not necessary for a woman to open up her hairs when taking Ghusl (bath) because of sexual relation.’”
